label: Schaeffer's concert of noises
detail: Pierre Schaeffer's "Cinq études de bruits", the first built from recordings of trains, is broadcast on French radio.

label: "The Flying Saucer"
detail: Buchanan and Goodman release a spoken skit with clips of current hits cut into it.

label: Mellotron Mark I
detail: The Bradley brothers of Birmingham start selling a tape-replay keyboard based on Harry Chamberlin's American design.

label: Clive Campbell moves to the Bronx
detail: The future DJ Kool Herc leaves Kingston, Jamaica, aged 12.

label: "Amen, Brother"
detail: The Winstons release it as the B-side of "Color Him Father"; G.C. Coleman plays the four-bar solo.

label: The Winstons release "Amen, Brother"
detail: Drummer Gregory Coleman plays the break; neither he nor copyright holder Richard Spencer received royalties from its later use.

label: "Funky Drummer"
detail: James Brown single, recorded in 1969, with Clyde Stubblefield's eight-bar break.

label: The "version" becomes standard
detail: Nearly every Jamaican single now carries an instrumental version on its B-side.

label: "Think (About It)"
detail: Lyn Collins on People Records, with Jabo Starks on drums.

label: "Apache" and "Impeach the President"
detail: The Incredible Bongo Band's Bongo Rock and The Honey Drippers' single both arrive.

label: First dub LPs
detail: Four albums released this year have each been called the first dub album, Lee "Scratch" Perry's "Blackboard Jungle Dub" among them.

label: Party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue
detail: DJ Kool Herc plays his sister Cindy Campbell's back-to-school party in the Bronx, extending drum breaks with two turntables.

label: Qasar M8
detail: Tony Furse's design, the basis of the Fairlight CMI.

label: Fairlight CMI
detail: Peter Vogel and Kim Ryrie demonstrate the first commercially available digital sampling instrument: 8-bit, 24 kHz.

label: "Rapper's Delight"
detail: The Sugarhill Gang's single is released, with a studio band replaying the bass and guitar of Chic's "Good Times"; Nile Rodgers says the strings were sampled.

label: Casio MT-40 and ESG's "UFO"
detail: The keyboard whose "rock" preset became Sleng Teng launches; ESG's EP comes out.

label: "Planet Rock" and "Change the Beat"
detail: Tommy Boy replays Kraftwerk; Celluloid presses the 12-inch with the "fresh" line.

label: "Planet Rock"
detail: Afrika Bambaataa & the Soulsonic Force's single replays Kraftwerk by hand and uses the Fairlight's stock orchestra hit.

label: "Rockit"
detail: GrandMixer D.ST scratches the "fresh" sample on Herbie Hancock's single.

label: Ensoniq Mirage
detail: A sampler at a reported $1,695, when an Emulator cost about $8,000.

label: "Under Mi Sleng Teng"
detail: Wayne Smith's single on Jammy's Records, built on a Casio preset.

label: Oswald names plunderphonics
detail: John Oswald publishes the essay "Plunderphonics, or Audio Piracy as a Compositional Prerogative".

label: Plunderphonics named
detail: John Oswald coins the word, in an essay, for music made openly from other recordings.

label: Ultimate Breaks and Beats begins
detail: The first Street Beat volumes appear; the Amen break is on volume 1.

label: Ultimate Breaks and Beats begins
detail: Lenny Roberts and BreakBeat Lou start a 25-volume series of break compilations that runs to 1990 or 1991.

label: "The Bridge"
detail: Marley Marl chops the kick, snare and hi-hat from "Impeach the President" for MC Shan.

label: "Pump Up the Volume" injunction
detail: Stock Aitken Waterman obtain an injunction over a seven-second sample in the M/A/R/R/S single; distribution stops for five days until a deal is reached.

label: E-mu SP-1200
detail: 12-bit, 26.04 kHz, 10 seconds of memory.

label: The JAMs' "1987"
detail: The future KLF release an album of long unlicensed samples; after ABBA complains, unsold copies are ordered destroyed.

label: "Pump Up the Volume"
detail: M/A/R/R/S release the single; an injunction over a seven-second sample halts distribution for five days.

label: "8 Volt Mix"
detail: DJ Battery Brain's Los Angeles single supplies the beat for 1990s funk carioca.

label: "8 Volt Mix"
detail: DJ Battery Brain's Los Angeles 12-inch comes out; its B-side beat becomes the base of 1990s funk carioca in Rio.

label: Akai MPC60
detail: Roger Linn's interface and David Cockerell's sound engine, at a reported $5,000.

label: The Turtles sue De La Soul
detail: Flo & Eddie sue over a 12-second sample on 3 Feet High and Rising. The case settles out of court with no ruling; the settlement year and amount are reported and unconfirmed.

label: "Paul's Boutique" clearance bill
detail: Engineer Mario Caldato Jr. later put the Beastie Boys' sample clearances at over $250,000, one participant's recollection.

label: 'Fish Market' riddim
detail: Steely & Clevie cut the Jamaican riddim that their lawsuit names as the source of reggaeton's dembow pattern.

label: "Paul's Boutique"
detail: The Beastie Boys and the Dust Brothers release an album with somewhere between 105 sampled songs and 300 samples, depending on who is counting.

label: Lawyers' letter reaches John Oswald
detail: The Canadian record industry's lawyers demand a halt to his free "Plunderphonic" CD; he settles and hands over his remaining copies.

label: Grand Upright v. Warner Bros.
detail: A New York federal court enjoins Biz Markie's "Alone Again" in the first US ruling on sampling.

label: Grand Upright v. Warner Bros. Records
detail: A federal court in New York grants an injunction over Biz Markie's "Alone Again" and finds a license was needed.

label: Ensoniq ASR-10
detail: The sampler RZA says the first 100 Wu-Tang songs were made on.

label: Campbell v. Acuff-Rose
detail: The US Supreme Court holds that a commercial parody can be fair use, in a case about 2 Live Crew and "Oh, Pretty Woman".

label: 'Trip hop' in print
detail: Mixmag's Andy Pemberton uses the term for DJ Shadow's 'In/Flux'; Portishead's 'Dummy' follows later in the year.

label: "Endtroducing....."
detail: DJ Shadow's album, which Guinness World Records lists as the first made completely from samples.

label: "Bitter Sweet Symphony" publishing goes to ABKCO
detail: After a late publishing request, ABKCO takes 100% of the song's publishing; Richard Ashcroft is paid a reported $1,000.

label: "I'll Be Missing You" released uncleared
detail: Puff Daddy's single uses "Every Breath You Take" without advance clearance; Sting later says he is paid $2,000 a day (his own claim, 2018).

label: Kraftwerk sue over "Nur mir"
detail: Kraftwerk's founders sue in Hamburg over Moses Pelham's 1997 loop of about two seconds of "Metall auf Metall", starting a case that was still in court in 2026.

label: 'Since I Left You'
detail: The Avalanches release their sample collage in Australia; it is usually put at more than 3,500 samples, and the 2001 international editions drop the ones that could not be cleared.

label: "Since I Left You"
detail: The Avalanches' album comes out in Australia after a delay for clearances; estimates of its sample count run from about 900 to over 3,500.

label: Boss SP-303
detail: Vinyl Sim and tape echo in a portable box.

label: Ableton Live 1
detail: Clips that stretch to the project tempo.

label: "Addictive" suits
detail: Saregama and Bappi Lahiri file suits over the Lata Mangeshkar sample.

label: Newton v. Diamond
detail: The Ninth Circuit holds the Beastie Boys' use of a three-note flute passage de minimis as to the composition.

label: Grey Tuesday
detail: About 170 websites host Danger Mouse's "The Grey Album" for a day in protest at EMI's stop order.

label: Bridgeport v. Dimension Films
detail: The Sixth Circuit holds there is no de minimis defense for digitally sampling a sound recording.

label: Roland SP-404
detail: 12 pads, 29 effects, CompactFlash.

label: G.C. Coleman dies
detail: The Amen break drummer dies without having received royalties for it.

label: "Donuts"
detail: J Dilla's 31-track album is released on his 32nd birthday; he dies three days later.

label: WhoSampled launches
detail: The user-submitted sample database goes live from London late in the year.

label: "Chuck Person's Eccojams Vol. 1"
detail: Daniel Lopatin collects his slowed, looped pop fragments, a founding record of vaporwave.

label: Kingsway Music Library starts
detail: Frank Dukes begins releasing original compositions made to be sampled, out of frustration with clearance.

label: UK pastiche exception
detail: Section 30A is added to the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act, permitting fair dealing for caricature, parody or pastiche.

label: J Dilla's MPC goes to the Smithsonian
detail: Maureen Yancey donates her son's MPC and custom Moog to the National Museum of African American History and Culture.

label: J Dilla's MPC3000 goes to the Smithsonian
detail: Maureen Yancey donates her son's MPC3000 Limited Edition and Minimoog Voyager.

label: Amen break crowdfund
detail: A GoFundMe run by two British DJs pays Richard Spencer; totals are given as £24,000 and as more than £18,000.

label: Amen Breakbeat Gesture
detail: Martyn Webster opens a GoFundMe for Richard Spencer; the page shows £24,000 raised.

label: VMG Salsoul v. Ciccone
detail: The Ninth Circuit holds a 0.23-second horn hit in Madonna's "Vogue" de minimis, splitting from Bridgeport.

label: Clyde Stubblefield dies
detail: The Funky Drummer dies of kidney failure at 73.

label: Tracklib launches
detail: The Swedish service sells original recordings with a release license of $50 to $2,500 and a revenue share of 2% to 50%, by press accounts.

label: Music Modernization Act signed
detail: US recordings made before February 15, 1972 get federal protection; those from 1957 onward are covered until 2067.

label: "Bitter Sweet Symphony" returned
detail: Richard Ashcroft announces Jagger and Richards have given up their credit and share.

label: Ashcroft gets "Bitter Sweet Symphony" back
detail: Richard Ashcroft announces that Mick Jagger and Keith Richards have signed over their share and dropped their credit.

label: "Acid Rap" reaches streaming without "Juice"
detail: Chance the Rapper's mixtapes arrive on streaming; one track is replaced by a placeholder over an unapproved sample.

label: CJEU, Pelham I
detail: The EU's top court holds a producer can object to even a very short sample unless it is unrecognizable to the ear.

label: Spleeter
detail: Deezer Research releases a free, open-source stem separator.

label: Estate of Smith v. Graham
detail: The Second Circuit affirms fair use for Drake's use of the "Jimmy Smith Rap" composition in "Pound Cake".

label: Primary Wave interpolation song camp
detail: More than two dozen writers spend three days near Los Angeles building new songs from old hits the publisher holds stakes in.

label: Paramore writers added to "Good 4 U"
detail: Hayley Williams and Josh Farro are credited on Olivia Rodrigo's single three months after release.

label: Tracklib counts 17% of Hot 100 songs with samples
detail: The company's count, which combines samples and interpolations, rises from 14% in 2021.

label: Sample drill gets a name in print
detail: Complex writes up New York drill built on recognizable R&B and pop samples.

label: Warhol v. Goldsmith
detail: The US Supreme Court narrows the first fair use factor, in an opinion that mentions sampling among uses that need a license.

label: De La Soul's first six albums reach streaming
detail: After a year of clearance work that began in January 2022, the catalog becomes legally available digitally for the first time.

label: 'Heart on My Sleeve' removed
detail: The AI voice-clone track imitating Drake and The Weeknd is pulled from streaming services after 629,439 Spotify streams.

label: EP-133 K.O. II
detail: Teenage Engineering's sampler launches at $299.

label: Warner Chappell v. Nealy
detail: The US Supreme Court holds there is no separate three-year cap on damages for a timely copyright claim.

label: An AI-generated sample is cleared
detail: Complex reports that 'U My Everything' samples the Udio-generated 'BBL Drizzy', cleared by licensing only the human-written publishing.

label: Ableton Live 12.3 beta
detail: Four-stem separation, processed locally, arrives in Live Suite.

label: Universal settles with Udio
detail: The first of three label settlements with AI music generators, with licenses and a joint platform planned for 2026.

label: Spotify buys WhoSampled
detail: Price undisclosed; the database then lists 1.2 million songs and 622,000 samples (company figures).

label: Warner settles with Suno
detail: Terms private; Suno agrees to launch licensed models and retire its current ones.

label: CJEU, Pelham II
detail: The Grand Chamber defines pastiche: sampling can qualify in principle, but only as a recognizable creative dialogue with the source.

label: Splice announces AI tools that pay sample creators
detail: New features built on more than 3 million licensed samples pay the original creator when a sound is used as a source.

label: "Amen, Brother" joins the National Recording Registry
detail: The Library of Congress names it one of 25 recordings in that year's class and credits Coleman by name for the six-second break.

label: GEMA v. Suno
detail: Munich Regional Court I rules largely for the German authors' society over six compositions; Suno appeals and the judgment is not final.

label: Dembow ruling
detail: In Browne v. Clark the judge grants the defendants summary judgment on the selection-and-arrangement theory; other claims continue.

label: German Federal Court of Justice, "Metall auf Metall"
detail: Applying Pelham II, the court holds the Kraftwerk loop a permitted pastiche from June 7, 2021.

label: Universal and Sony sue Suno again
detail: A second suit in Massachusetts federal court covers 60,202 recordings and Suno's v6 models, after a judge declined to add them to the 2024 case.
